item.title: Re: Thank you :)
item.content:encoded:
Hi promethcookie! I noticed a few very common mistakes in your draft, such as overuse of text formatting such as underlining, inserting lines to add space when formatting exists that can add blank line breaks, and using imperial measurements in some places and metric in others. On top of that, there were a large number of spelling and grammar errors, especially in the interview at the end. You also need to make sure that any images you include in your SCP are compliant with the Creative Commons Share-Alike 3.0 license - which I assume an edited photo of a nun costume is not - or else it will be removed from the article.

For first-time wiki contributors, it's recommended that you seek critique on the forums before posting. The ideas forum is a great place to start to get your core idea critiqued before moving on to the drafting phase, then to get critique on your draft and post once it is polished.

None of this is mandatory, but most new contributors find a much greater chance of success going this route.

item.title: Re: Corpse of a Dead God
item.content:encoded:
Great write-up, but this is just the beginning.

1) The basic problem is that there is no visible SCP involvement. Even if it is just cursory that needs to be allowed for somewhere, be it an inspection by a Foundation agent, temporary control, or some other option. It's even possible for someone close to the CEO to a double-agent and feeding information to The Foundation; given his interest in the occult, it's a good fit.

2) There's far too much mystery here. What happened to him and his followers is of interest, and it needs to be given a reason of some sort. It doesn't matter if they became animals themselves, become a copse, have just decided to create a mystery cult to defend the body from others, or even another force has started eliminated everyone for the body, but their fate needs to be drawn out or at least hinted at.

Again, overall this is great write-up. There are some minor grammatical errors, but otherwise it's a good start!

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: I just listened to TheVolgun’s fantastic audio rendition of SCP-2137 and was very fascinated with the article as a whole.

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

Additional Notes: I’m returning to the SCP wiki after a fairly long absence so I’m sure there are things I’ve missed. I originally formatted this post wrong because last time I posted here no such thing existed. So if this idea has been done, or if it’s very similar to another tale, please let me know!

item.title: Lonely voice
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Fantasy, and Supernatural

Elevator Pitch: Basically, it's a voice that talks to you when you're alone, separate from any other human contact for a time. It starts as your own thoughts, and diverges from your normal train of thought without your notice. Some people are more inclined to hear it, even when around others, but it talks to anyone separate from humanity for an extended period of time.

Central Narrative: It starts with a psych patient being evaluated for possible anomaly, but a suggestion by one of scientist puts forward the idea that an SCP may be attracted to the situation the patient was in—he had lived alone for many years, secluded. Tests are done putting people in isolation, and many attest to a divergence of thought from their normal thoughts after a time. This is chalked up to normal psychological phenomena, until patterns are seen in the thought patterns: many suggest being drawn away to be separate from humanity, such as going to isolated geographical places, as well as questioning social norms. Several of the test subjects are found to be heading to isolated areas in forests, and atop buildings over following weeks. Basically, the scientists come to the conclusion that the source of the thoughts are voices coming from a variety of non physical beings that dwell in places less inhabited by humans.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact that it's relatable.

Additional Notes: Ehm, as a possible addition to the narrative, these beings are speculated to be aiding it trying to separate humans from each other one by one, as to aid in making an easier invasion of their own species.

item.title: Re: Skeleton's Daycare
item.content:encoded:
Hello Koke Ghoul! let's take a look :)

The concept:

It's a daycare owned by a living skeleton. The skeleton itself isn't anomalous, it's just a normal human who decomposed into a skeleton but is still alive due to some immortality crystals on the walls of the daycare.

The only other people in the daycare are alien children. For the most part, they're fairly normal. They have a bit of a temper, and they're capable of causing minor earthquakes, so you might not wanna anger them too badly.

My main issue here is the earthquakes, the effect as a whole doesn't really seem related to anything, and (at least to me) takes focus away from the narratives overall theme. Currently, it comes off as a way to make the 'aliens', more dangerous and/or quickly make them more interesting.

+ show block
– hide block

The narrative:

This daycare used to be pretty normal. Then these alien parents came in and had to drop their kids off because "they had to do something." When they left the kids at the daycare, they left them with some crystals that would make them and anyone near the crystals immortal.

Two people used to run the daycare, but the original owner left to go find the parents because they've been gone for way too long and they can't close without all the kids leaving. This left the other guy to run it all by himself, but the owner was out for so long that the other guy's body became a skeleton.

After some time, one of the alien parents came back and took their kid, along with one of the crystals. This caused the skeleton's life to become much harder. This, along with the stress of taking care of aliens, was adding up. Then more of the alien parents came in to take their kid and their crystal. It got worse and worse.

At some point, the skeleton couldn't take it anymore and just left the building, causing him to die from getting out of range from the crystals. The children were attached to him after living there for a long time, so they tried to bring him inside and get him to live again, but it didn't work. Remember in the Elevator Pitch how the kids could cause minor earthquakes? They're really upset now, and they're causing serious damage to the rest of the world. They tried calming them down, but nothing would work. Because of the danger, they had to put them into a comatose state and look for their parents quickly. It then ends with the Foundation contacting the original owner who explains that the rest of the parents are long gone. Neutralization was the only other option.

While I do like the narratives main theme and conflict, there are some things that don't really add up, or aren't really explained in enough detail. Here are my main issues (in no particular order);

-there isn't much showing how the Foundation came across the skip, or how they get all of this information. Especially considering the care taker ends up dead before before the Foundation finds anything.

-the narrative pitch as a whole doesn't really give a strong idea of how this would fit in a draft, as the Foundation doesn't seem involved much.- do note the article is being written from their perspective.

- The timeline feels very off, considering the co-owner has already died and decayed, by the time his/her colleague comes back/gets questioned by the Foundation.- along with this, there isn't anything that explains why the owner never came back (at least not in the expected timeframe).

-It also feels odd that no-one ever checked into the daycare after this event? or even thought to contact them? what about the owners family or friends?

-As it stands, there doesn't seem to be much of a reason why the 'aliens', continuously take the crystals away, (or why the crystals were implemented to begin with, did the skips plan to leave their children forever?). Or, why they chose this place in particular to leave their children.- what exactly did they need to do? and why/how did they (presumably) die or abandon their children?

-The Foundation feels a bit out of character, considering they decide to kill the skips in the end.-why can't they be kept in comatose?

-How does the 'skeletons' mental state decline? currently the narrative doesn't give enough detail on what the character was like, what he struggled with and how everything started becoming harder. I as the reader can't really get invested, as there's not much about the character to relate to or really feel for.
- Along with this, the skip(s) themselves don't really seem to have of a place in the narrative either, how do they react to everything? how do they affect the overall story?

Closing thoughts:
Currently the ending doesn't really hit me very hard, as I never really got any time to get invested in the skips or their care taker. I feel the narrative could work better if you focused a bit more on the characters and their conflicts, and gave the aliens's parents a clearer motive/reason for leaving their children.

Along with this, you might be better off scraping the crystals altogether. As they only really complicate the timeline, and take focus away from the skips themselves.- the care taker can still have the same conflicts and issues, without becoming a skeleton.

Red or green?
Due to mu afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques/perspectives in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

RED

item.title: Gossip Ghost
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Default, with exposition mostly delivered through fragments on the conversations the program had with its victims.

Elevator Pitch: There's a program in the internet that's going around revealing people's secrets, the only way to take its unrelenting attention from you is revealing something it deems more interesting than what it had to say about you. This program is looking for someone it deems as its main target, someone that did it wrong in the past, a foundation employee, a researcher, or guard, or another D-class(Purposefully kept unclear), and the information it deems interesting is something it can use to blackmail someone that gets it closer to its target. The program is in a way the reincarnation of a foundation employee, most likely a D-class killed in an experiment accident where there is no clear cut case as to who is the real culprit.

Central Narrative: The SCP speaks in a child-like manner and is single-minded in getting what it wants, it initially only communicates its blackmail secrets by going, "Did you know that X did Y on the thursday night of winter[And adds more very specific details, so that the current victim knows it knows something it shouldn't] The scp doesn't have perfect information, but is able to tell what the victim wants to keep secret the most, or the top-5, top-10 things they want to keep secret, that rarely is the information it -wants- so it uses that as a means to an end.

Hook: The goal of the scp is somewhat of a mistery up until the middle of the conversation logs, so that would keep the reader guessing what is it that it wants, the fact that it wants something specific is made clear from the beginning of the article.

item.title: Re: Guidance to the oblivious (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I'm a little confused about the anomaly itself. What is doing this? What are the prerequisite factors for its intervention? Is there something intelligent behind this anomaly? If so, what is their reasoning? Why wouldn't this anomaly attempt to hide itself from the Foundation?

Then, we look through the list of incidents it took place in (about 8 ~ 15 I haven't found the goldilocks number to form a pattern or a narrative yet, officially in the record, it would be around a few thousand).

I think you wanna be careful, as this seems like too many to me. I'd keep it to like 5 examples, and make them really sing… then with some follow up, explaining that in all recorded instances only 35% were successful. But if you're going to tee up the fact that this anomaly isn't very successful (as this is pretty poor result) what are you going to do with that in the article?

item.content:encoded:
• Could you please elaborate on when it's a good time to use logs? I personally always liked them and some of my favourite SCPs have extensive logs. I was hoping to have a log of the experiments in a brief format, generally "What the bone was from, who touched it and what happened", which I hoped could be interesting with some of the results.
  • That's fair. It was to generally show that the SCP isn't 100% there, but that can be done in other, more subtle ways.
  • I'm afraid you lost me in this part, most likely due to my lack of experience. What exactly do you mean by a climax? I'm not sure how to get a resolution in a document, or how an SCP that is by the Foundation's standards fairly mundane could upset the status quo of a reader who's used to far more extreme anomalies.

One of the guides I read, specifically this one goes into how a typical narrative arc isn't plausible in what is a document with no progression of time. I'd appreciate it if you could explain this part a bit more to me.

item.title: Re: Smile!
item.content:encoded:
Some small stuff concerning your use of "[REDACTED]" and "[EXPUNGED]."

[+] Open
[-] Close

"he was then [REDACTED]." how am I supposed to be scared of this thing when you are basically saying "something scary happens here, trust me!"

"the members of the cult started to [REDACTED]." same issue as above.

"a bench in the city of [REDACTED]" frankly this is just unnecessary, choose any city in the world and it would work better (imo) than "[REDACTED]."

To expunge is to erase or remove completely, according to what you have written: nobody, not even the O5, knows or is able to know what the subject begins to do.

Here's a great piece about the modern use of redaction on the SCP wiki by MalyceGraves that I highly recommend you read through: http://scp-wiki.wikidot.com/avoid-the-blackbox

item.title: Re: The Laughing Tree
item.content:encoded:
I agree.

Neither the name writing or suicide existed in the previous iteration. Instead, being tied to the tree meant disappearing weeks later. Plainly, I went from a cliche to something over the top.

I'm struggling with two parts of this concept:

  1. What happens after being tied to the tree
  2. How the survivor escaped
+ show block
– hide block

For the first, I want the names to be written on the tree. And I kinda want the victim to return to it. The name-writing is meant to represent the emotional scaring this event has on the victim. … What if the camp staff interview reveals that the he knew about the SCP and had even been one of it's victims in the past? Instead of killing/disappearing people, it causes them to laugh & enjoy the pain of others?

For the second, (at the moment) I just have the tree disgusted by urine and a victim that wets himself. To be clear, this would never be explicitly stated. I want the escape method to be embarrassing & uncomfortable, and an "accident" seems to fit. Any thoughts?

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Man in the Mirror
item.content:encoded:
So, 1) I don't see an anomaly actually discussed. Sure you're hinting they just appeared… but there's no specific anomaly at least as how it stands. Do you have an answer? I would suggest making that clear in the post…

2) I think this would work better as a tale, formatted to read as dueling reports from each organization, finally revealing why it matters to the Foundation or vice versa, that the other exists.

3) I think you're missing stakes/a stinger here. At the end, this is just another GOI that wants the same thing as the Foundation… So why are you interested in telling this story? What's the ultimate point you're trying to make? As if its merely "other SCP like orgs exist" then I don't see this being satisfying in the end.

I have to say that cybersqyd's suggestion that these are really the same org, and the ultimate revelation is that this has been a mismanagement of an org (foundation) that has just gotten too big to efficiently run its own affairs… that's fascinating.
